questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Portugal?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Portugal article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Portugal?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Portugal on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Portugal article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by the North Atlantic Ocean to the west and south and by Spain to the north and east.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Portugal is a popular holiday destination but is sometimes overlooked in favor of larger countries like _____, Spain and Italy.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Spain”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Portugal article.

questions.proof: Portugal is a popular holiday destination but is sometimes overlooked in favor of larger countries like France, Spain and Italy.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Portugal became a kingdom in _____ but was not officially recognized until 1143.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twelfth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Kingdom of Portugal” part of the Portugal article.

questions.proof: Portugal became a kingdom in 1139 but was not officially recognized until 1143.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Portugal and Spain were in the Iberian Union from _____ to 1640.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the sixteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Kingdom of Portugal” part of the Portugal article.

questions.proof: Portugal and Spain were in the Iberian Union from 1580 to 1640.
